Fun, silly, and most importantly; it is something I can play with my 4 year old daughter. The amount of freedom it allows her, is perfect for anyone her age. Lots to explore and lots of secrets.

I also believe there are some valuable life lessons for children to learn from this game. For instance, it teaches the value of money and to have a work ethic. You actually have to do jobs to make money. My daughter won't stop buying things; specifically silly hats, jello, and ice cream. She then proceeds to ask why we can't go to space. I keep telling her it costs $500 to go to space. I am hoping her desire to go to space will teach her the importance of holding a steady job and not spending money like a 4 year old. She hasn't quite figured that out yet.

Honestly though, pretty great game with lots to do.

Honestly, Wobbly Life is one of the most fun games I have ever played. My little brother absolutely loves this game and plays it all the time. Watching him enjoy it made me want to try it myself, and I was genuinely impressed.

The game is incredibly entertaining and never feels boring. The missions are fun and challenging at the same time, which keeps you motivated to continue and complete everything. Playing it together with my brother made the experience even better. We had so many fun moments trying to finish the missions.

I only have two missions left to complete the game 100%, and I have enjoyed every part of it so far. I truly recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun and enjoyable experience. You will not regret playing it.

Basic Review: Light-hearted open-world life-sim with the perfect touch of humour. We have at least 50 big-title games across Steam and Nintendo but this is the first game our son has loved. The 3 of us have been waking up excited to play it and at the end of the day we rush home still excited to play, THATS true awesomeness! 10/10 (And i NEVER say that)
​
OFFICIAL REVIEW:
I've been gaming for 28 years but I can honestly say Wobbly Life has created a world with more genuine diversity and heart than almost anything I’ve ever played.
​
This game features the exact things kids actually dream of doing - firefighting, police, farming, astronauts, ambulances, mining, garbage, tree lopping just to name a few. None of it feels half-done, the devs treated these roles with care and respect, so the work feels like it actually matters.

The devs included little pictures in the menus so kids can "read" and 'play it all by myself'.
​
Most games are full of "No, not yet sorry dude" or "Not in this game sorry bud" where-as Wobbly Life is; "Yes actually, you CAN do that," which completely prevents the deflated feelings for sensitive kids.

The ability to use a mini-mod trainer in arcade-mode environment is brilliant. My 4-year-old can hit R3, spawn 400 bouncing balls or dynamites, and go absolutely mental without the game crashing, creating a safe space for total chaos - mad healthy for a young mind.
​
Our son is happy to play solo, but the second we get home, yelling "Two-player Wobbly Life!"

100% Wobbly Life on 3/31/2024. My wife and I fully beat this game and enjoyed the entire trip. This sandbox game can be described as GTA but without all the violence and maybe a bit more Wobbly. It is such a fun open world game, with tons of vehicles, customizations, tasks, quests and it has up to four player coop. There are some luck based aspects and admittedly collecting $10000 and  every fish for those specific achievements took quite a while; but we got them in the end. There is also a workshop with tons of custom made levels; however, these are very much hit or miss. With all that being said, we wish we could go back and play it all over again with fresh memories. 

(Note: Since getting 100%, many more free updates have released, including an expansive space update which was so fun and felt like a brand new game. Sadly with all the new free updates also came an update that finished the museum and added an achievement to fully complete the museum. This wouldn't be so bad if it wasn't for a chunk of the museum artifacts requiring luck to find in the treasure hunter jobs. These treasure hunter jobs are annoying and completely random on whether you get a new artifact, junk or an artifact you already got which is essentially junk. This is what is still preventing us from getting 100% again. The developers added quality of life updates to help find all the presents, they need to do the same thing for these treasure hunter artifacts.)

TL;DR: Very fun with friends, not as fun alone. The grabbing mechanic can sometimes be frustrating, and so can parkour. But the game has a lot to offer and is overall a great time with friends, and I've really enjoyed playing it. 
 
This is a very fun game to play with a couple of friends. There are several different quests and jobs to do, places to explore, and things to unlock. Adding friends into the mix makes it much less lonely and significantly more chaotic. Parkour in the game can be a little frustrating at times, as well as the grabbing mechanic (the amount of times I've meant to hit a button or pick up an item but grabbed the wall instead is too many to count), but overall the enjoyability of the game outweighs the frustration. I think this is a game best played with multiple people, so I would say if you and a small group of friends are all interested, definitely give it a go, but if it would just be you by yourself playing it may not be as fun.
